transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-17 09:32 PT | Duration: 45 min | Attendees: Jordan Fields (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Summit AI - CTO), Priya Patel (Lead ML Eng), Samir Khan (DevOps), Jamie Lee (PM)

Summary: Quick PLG-style discovery focused on Redwood self-serve API (quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token) and whether Summit AI should start with Hosted or move to Dedicated/Private for compliance and latency reasons. Customer is evaluating speed to prototype and cost predictability for a pilot customer-facing assistant.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. we also have Maya our solutions engineer. quick pulse — is this still a 45 minute slot?
[00:12] Alex: yep that's right, thanks Jordan. i'm Alex, CTO at Summit AI. Priya and Samir are on to cover ML and infra.
[00:20] Priya: hi, thanks. we're mostly looking at the self-serve quickstart, free credits, and how fast we can get to first token, also curious about Dedicated for lower latency.
[00:34] Maya: great — i'll take the technical bits. quick overview: Redwood's PLG quickstart is typically a few minutes to sign up and spin up an API key, examples for node/python, and we provide free credits for trial evals. timing to first token is usually sub-second for short prompts on hosted for many models, but depends on model/seq length.
[00:52] Samir: when you say sub-second, is that median p99? like our SLAs, we care about p95/p99.
[00:58] Maya: good call — for the hosted plans p50 can be sub-second for smaller models, p95 might be 200-400ms on optimized Gen-like models, p99 higher depending on concurrency and model. Dedicated pools give more predictable p95/p99 since you reserve GPU capacity.
[01:18] Priya: what's the onboarding— is it literally self-serve? do we need sales to enable Dedicate, or can we try Hosted first?
[01:25] Jordan: it's PLG-first. you can sign up, get free credits, and hit the API. Dedicated is a sales-assisted step — typically after you've validated with Hosted or if you have immediate compliance needs.
[01:36] Alex: we have an enterprise customer who requires SOC 2 and data residency in eu-west. we might need a private deployment down the line. how does Private work? VPC or on-prem?
[01:46] Maya: Private supports customer VPC and on-prem options. for eu residency we can do a private control plane in their region and integrate KMS/HSM for key management. we also integrate with SSO (SAML/Okta) and provide audit logs.
[02:01] Jamie: is that a separate install or a managed private offering?
[02:05] Maya: it's a managed private control plane with options for customer-managed networking; fully on-prem is available for air-gapped needs but that is a different track.
[02:13] Priya: ok good. latency wise — if we start on Hosted to iterate, then move to Dedicated for our pilot, is there friction in model versions or API changes?
[02:23] Maya: same API surface — we keep the same REST/SDK interface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, so moving between them is mostly config and routing. model versions can be pinned. some perf tuning like batching, cache config, and quantization profiles are per-deployment though.
[02:38] Alex: what's the cost delta? Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated has reserved commit — how do we forecast?
[02:44] Jordan: Hosted is per-token/embedding. Dedicated is monthly commit with better unit economics and predictable throughput — we can share an example cost spreadsheet showing break-even points for your QPS. i'll send that after.
[02:57] Samir: security question — does hosted persist logs or inputs? our data policy says no customer PII can be logged.
[03:03] Maya: we have data retention controls, can opt-out of retaining request payloads for hosted evals, and Dedicated/Private gives full control of logs and retention. we support customer-managed KMS.
[03:13] Priya: another technical: we do heavy use of caching and want prefix KV cache. how does Redwood handle KV caches and batching?
[03:21] Maya: runtime supports KV cache management and automatic prefix caching; we also do continuous batching and dynamic kernel selection for performance. Priya: mhmm (short) ok.
[03:31] Alex: what's the fastest way for Priya to try with her prompt set? do you recommend a sandbox?
[03:36] Jordan: sign up and use the quickstart repo — it includes a small harness. we'll give you free credits that are enough to run a couple of benchmarks with your prompt set.
[03:45] Priya: excellent. i want to test quality regressions — do you have eval tooling or tie-ins?
[03:50] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize gives quality monitoring and regression alerts, we can run evals on your prompt sets and set baselines. for quick trials we can do a manual eval and show simple metrics (BLEU-ish, similarity, custom scoring).
[04:03] [04:03] Alex: competitor check — we've been chatting with Anthropic and exploring OpenAI for baseline; curious how Redwood compares on throughput + cost.
[04:11] Jordan: common question; Redwood focuses on production economics — we can show throughput benchmarks for open models and cost recommendations like quantization and batching to reduce unit token cost.
[04:22] Priya: i'd like a sense of how much time you'd need to run a real benchmark with our prompts — is an hour enough?
[04:27] Maya: depends on sample size; a representative run for latency + correctness with 500-1k prompts is enough to show trends. we can set up a 1-hour benchmark run for p95/p99 with your dataset.
[04:36] Samir: infra constraints — our infra is AWS with EKS and we prefer VPC peering for private deployments. are there network requirements?
[04:44] Maya: we support VPC peering and peered private control plane. firewall rules and egress are standard; we'll send a network checklist.
[04:51] Jamie: timeline — we're hoping to ship a pilot in Q4, so we want a vendor selected by early october. is that realistic?
[04:58] Jordan: absolutely — start with Hosted quickstart this week, run the benchmark next week, if all looks good we can scope Dedicated/Private commitment and timeline.
[05:07] Priya: questions about model variants — do you host both base open models and tuned variants? and do you allow function calling and streaming?
[05:15] Maya: we host a curated catalog, including open base models and some Redwood-verified variants; function/tool calling and streaming are supported via the same API.
[05:24] Alex: for the pilot, we probably need end-to-end security review. can you share SOC 2 and network diagrams?
[05:29] Jordan: yes i will send SOC 2 reports, sample network diagrams, and the security pack.
[05:34] Priya: a nit — how do you handle rate limits for PLG accounts? we don't want our devs throttled while testing.
[05:41] Jordan: PLG accounts have soft limits with easy lift via the console; for higher QPS you can request increased quotas or move to Dedicated.
[05:47] Samir: any gotchas with tokenization differences across models? we rely on consistent token counts for cost forecasting.
[05:55] Maya: tokenization differs by model family — we can help map cost per effective token for the models you'll run. we'll suggest model/quant profiles to match quality/cost.
[06:06] [06:06] Priya: let's talk about expected pilot scale metrics: for our pilot we expect 100 rps at peak, typical prompt lengths about 120 tokens, and tight 95th latency goals. does Dedicated handle 100 rps?
[06:16] Maya: depends on model and GPU size; Dedicated with correct pool sizing plus batching typically hits that with headroom. we'll size a recommended Dedicated pool in the follow-up.
[06:26] Alex: i'm also curious about multi-region failover — if eu region has an outage, do you support automatic routing to other regions while respecting data residency?
[06:33] Maya: we have smart routing policies; for strict residency we'd failover to compatible models in the same region. if allowed, we can route to another region, but we'll respect your policy.
[06:44] Jordan: i'll recap — action items and next steps, we'll send pricing/credits, quickstart repo, security docs, and schedule a benchmark. any blockers?
[06:52] Priya: only that we need sample prompts and permission to run them in your hosted eval.
[06:57] Jordan: noted, Priya will share prompts.
[07:00] [07:00] Alex: timeline again — i'll want a short SLA for Dedicated, what's typical?
[07:06] Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; exact numbers depend on the contract tier, but we can share standard SLAs.
[07:13] Samir: and monitoring — do you expose per-route token cost and traces?
[07:19] Maya: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, traces, and can export to your observability stack.
[07:27] Priya: for benchmarking, will we be able to replicate KV cache behavior? some prompts benefit a lot from prefix cache which affects latency greatly.
[07:35] Maya: good point — we can enable prefix/KV caching in the benchmark to measure realistic p95.
[07:41] Jordan: anything else on migration — we try to make rolling to Dedicated easy, but quantization and kernel tuning sometimes require a short tuning pass.
[07:49] Priya: that's fine.
[07:51] [07:51] Jamie: decision-makers — final approval will be Alex + procurement, timeline is early october, budget TBD.
[07:59] Jordan: i'll include procurement checklist in the follow-up.
[08:04] [08:04] Alex: sounds good. one more small question: can we get a sandbox account per developer or shared account? our devs like per-person dev keys.
[08:12] Jordan: you can create multiple API keys per account and set RBAC, or create separate org-level workspaces. we'll point you to the console.
[08:20] Priya: great. ok let's schedule the benchmark — mornings next week are best for us.
[08:25] Maya: i'll follow up with an invite and a dataset checklist.
[08:29] Jordan: thanks everybody — quick recap of next steps in the notes and i'll send everything over.
[08:36] Alex: thanks — excited to test.

End of transcript. Note: some ASR artifacts present (e.g., "Dedicate" instead of Dedicated, 'KV cache' might be written as 'K V cache' etc.).
